sources.quote: Toronto's Private Tree By-law requires a permit to remove or injure a private tree 30 cm or more in diameter at 1.4 m
sources.title: When to Apply For a Tree or Ravine Permit – City of Toronto
sources.evidence: Any activity that can cause a tree of 30 centimetres or more in diameter, to be injured or removed, on private property, is prohibited unless authorized with a permit under the Tree Protection By-law. The diameter is measured 1.4 m (4.5 ft) above the ground.

sources.quote: Vancouver's Protection of Trees By-law sets 20 cm and generally allows removal only of dead, hazardous or construction-blocking trees, with replacement planting or cash in lieu
sources.title: Get a tree removal permit | City of Vancouver
sources.evidence: You don't need a permit to remove a tree that is smaller than 20 centimetres in diameter unless the tree was previously identified as a replacement tree. Property owners may be granted permission to remove trees if the tree on a development site is located within the building envelope, or an arborist certifies the tree is dead, dying, or hazardous. A replacement tree will be required to be planted for any removed tree that is larger than 20 centimetres diameter.

sources.quote: Ottawa uses 30 cm in the inner urban area
sources.title: General information - Tree Protection By-law | City of Ottawa
sources.evidence: Under the Tree Protection By-law, all distinctive trees (trees 30 cm or more in diameter at breast height on private properties within the urban area that are 1 hectare or less in size) are protected trees that cannot be injured or removed without a tree permit from the City.

sources.quote: Montreal is stricter again: a felling permit is generally required at 10 cm
sources.title: Demander un permis d'abattage d'arbre sur un terrain privé | Ville de Montréal
sources.evidence: Vous devez vous procurer un permis pour abattre un arbre dont le tronc a au moins 10 cm de diamètre, mesuré à 1,3 m du sol ou un diamètre de 15 cm, mesuré à 15 cm du sol. Vous devez remplacer l'arbre abattu dans les 6 mois suivant l'abattage.

sources.quote: Alberta bans elm pruning province-wide from April 1 to September 30
sources.title: Dutch Elm Disease – Prevention and control | Alberta.ca
sources.evidence: To help keep Alberta Dutch elm disease (DED) free, there is a provincial elm pruning ban between April 1 and September 30. Elm bark beetles, the vectors of DED, are active between these dates and can be attracted to the scent of fresh tree cuts. Pruning elms can only be carried out commencing October 1 to March 31 the following year.

sources.title: Province of Manitoba | DED Questions & Answers
sources.evidence: It is illegal to prune elms from April 1 to July 31, when the beetles are the most active. If a limb is badly damaged and poses an immediate risk to safety, it can be removed during the ban if approved by the Forestry Branch.

sources.title: Dutch Elm Disease | Forest Health | Government of Saskatchewan
sources.evidence: The provincial pruning ban is in place from April 1 to August 31 each year to help curb the spread of Dutch elm disease (DED). In Saskatchewan, anyone who prunes elm trees commercially must have completed a provincially recognized training program or be supervised by someone who has.

sources.quote: Canadian Food Inspection Agency orders restrict moving ash material and firewood out of regulated areas
sources.title: Regulated areas and items: Emerald ash borer - inspection.canada.ca
sources.evidence: The movement of ash products out of regulated areas in Canada has restrictions at the domestic level. Moving ash firewood out of a regulated area is prohibited, whether for commercial or private purposes. Regulated items moving out of a regulated area must be accompanied by a Movement Certificate issued by the Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA).

sources.quote: with corporate penalties reaching CAD 10 million or three times the benefit derived
sources.title: Penalties and remedies for non-compliance
sources.evidence: For corporations, the penalty for a first-time violation is up to the greater of: $10 million ($15 million for each subsequent violation); and three times the value of the benefit derived from the deceptive conduct, or, if that amount cannot be reasonably determined, 3% of the corporation's annual worldwide gross revenue.

sources.quote: Implied consent runs 6 months from an estimate inquiry and 2 years from a completed job
sources.title: Frequently Asked Questions about Canada's Anti-Spam Legislation | CRTC
sources.evidence: You may have an existing business relationship if the recipient has made a purchase or lease of goods, services, land or interest in land within the two-year period immediately before the message was sent, or if the recipient has made an inquiry or application within the six month period immediately before the message was sent.

sources.quote: note that Google folded its trust badges into one verified badge in late 2025
sources.title: About Google Verified badge - Local Services Help
sources.evidence: Local Services Ads will be simplifying badging by launching a single, more cohesive Google Verified badge for all advertisers effective October 20, 2025. Google will discontinue all existing Local Services Ads badges, including Google Guaranteed, Google Screened, and License Verified by Google, effective October 20, 2025.
